prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single perfect site that does plain‑English beginner guides, publishes raw on‑chain numbers, and also posts an audited record of its own losses — but you can get exactly what you want by combining a plain‑English education source with some transparent data and post‑mortem sites. Recommended combo:

- Plain‑English beginner guides (easy to read, good explanations)
  - Coin Bureau — excellent beginner guides and YouTube explainers in plain language.
  - Decrypt — news + explainers written for newcomers.
  - Bankless — plain English DeFi education (newsletter and podcasts).

- Sites that show real numbers / on‑chain data (verify claims yourself)
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards that show raw numbers for protocols, TVL, flows; very transparent.
  - Glassnode Studio / CryptoQuant — curated on‑chain charts and explanations.
  - Coin Metrics / Token Terminal — market and fundamental data with raw tables.

- Sites that publish losses, hacks and post‑mortems
  - REKT (rekt.news) — catalog of hacks, rug pulls and loss amounts; good for understanding real failures.
  - Chainalysis blog & reports — data‑driven post‑mortems and quantified loss estimates from scams/hacks.
  - The Defiant often publishes post‑mortems and coverage of major losses in DeFi.

Practical suggestion: start with a plain‑English guide (Coin Bureau or Decrypt) to learn the concepts, then cross‑check any investment or protocol claims on Dune/Glassnode/Nansen and look up past exploits on REKT/Chainalysis to see downside history. If you want, tell me which area you’re focused on (investing, trading, DeFi yield, NFTs) and I’ll give a 3–5 item curated reading/list of dashboards and post‑mortems tailored to that.
